title: Improved Quantification of Ocean Carbon Uptake by Using Machine Learning to Merge Global Models and pCO2 Data
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: The study produces an observation-model merged reconstruction of surface ocean pCO2 and air-sea CO2 fluxes using XGBoost; it is not a high-resolution simulation dataset or testbed designed for training or evaluating ML-based atmospheric or oceanic parameterizations.
pain_points: Severe spatial and temporal data sparsity of in situ surface ocean carbon observations, especially in the Southern Ocean and earlier decades (1980s).
Temporal skewness in the target variable (pCO2) due to secular climate warming and anthropogenic carbon increase, which degrades statistical/ML algorithm generalization.
Systematic biases in dynamical GOBM simulations (e.g., omitting the water vapor correction in atmospheric pCO2 forcing, biases in seasonal mixed-layer dynamics).
extraction_notes: The paper presents the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory - Hybrid Physics Data (LDEO-HPD) methodology that predicts model-data misfit between 9 GOBMs and SOCAT observations using XGBoost, then adds predicted misfits back to the GOBMs to produce a full spatiotemporal ocean pCO2 product.
